outgoing.name: Cretaceous
outgoing.excerpt: Sauroposeidon was a sauropod from the Early Cretaceous Period, related to the more famous Brachiosaurus.

outgoing.name: Deity
outgoing.excerpt: The Greek sea-god Poseidon was also known as Ennosigaios or Enisokhthōn = "Earthshaker".

outgoing.name: England
outgoing.excerpt: A giant brachiosaurid, similar to Sauroposeidon, was described in 2004 by Darren Naish and colleagues and is from the Early Cretaceous period of England.

outgoing.name: Fossil
outgoing.excerpt: Supersaurus and Argentinosaurus are better candidates for the title "World's Largest Dinosaur", though weak fossil evidence makes an exact ranking impossible.

outgoing.name: Greek mythology
outgoing.excerpt: The genus name comes from sauros ( Greek for "lizard"), and Poseidon, a sea-god in Greek mythology, who is also associated with earthquakes.

outgoing.name: North America
outgoing.excerpt: Sauroposeidon may be the last of the giant North American sauropods.
